A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive rewriting, renaming, and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-editing experiments, component ablations, hyperparameter sensitivity results, and GPT-4V and human evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds SDXL results, additional temperature evaluations, and a batched-runtime measurement.

M1.justification: Concept Distillation Sampling renames the existing Optimised DDS plus multi-LoRA framework. Ordered timesteps, regularisation, negative guidance, and cosine-similarity-based SoftMin fusion remain equivalent. Explicit SoftMin normalisation and batched prediction explain implementations of the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover InstructPix2Pix and ComposLoRA-style anime and realistic editing, including multiple concepts and pose/expression changes. The SDXL addition evaluates an existing two-concept editing task with another backbone; it does not establish a distinct task or data domain.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and the retained qualitative comparisons use the same methods, including DiffusionClip, PnP, InstructPix2Pix, DDS, PDS, Composite, Switch, and Merge. The new SDXL experiment reuses Merge. DreamCatalyst and LoRWeB are newly discussed but are not evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 adds an SDXL configuration at N=2, evaluates temperatures 0.01 and 0.1, and reports runtime with batched LoRA predictions. The existing experiments retain their stated sample selection, metrics, guidance settings, 300 optimisation steps, and hardware.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds a backbone-generalisation check with numerical and qualitative SDXL evidence. Table 7 expands temperature sensitivity beyond the original two endpoints, and Section 6 adds a batching comparison. Existing component ablations, regularisation and patch-size analyses, and pose examples remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over three runs, the same uncertainty entries and 99% significance convention, reversed-order GPT-4V comparisons, and Kendall agreement of 0.68. No additional statistical procedure or increased run count is documented; the new SDXL table contains point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing main-table and GPT-4V scores are unchanged. v3 Table 8 adds SDXL CLIPScore/LPIPS results of 0.304/0.21 for CDS versus 0.273/0.38 for Merge. Table 7 adds two temperature-result rows, and Section 6 reports 33 seconds with batching alongside the retained 44-second sequential runtime. These additions concern new configurations.

T1.justification: v3 omits the explicit PDS gradient and source/target forward-noising definitions in v1 Equations 3–5, shortening the mathematical background. The proposed optimisation and fusion equations remain equivalent, and expanding the SoftMin formula introduces no new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: v3 refines the novelty claim to explicitly target-less, reference-free multi-concept editing, highlighting the absence of desired-edit reference samples. The principal claims of unified training-free editing, concept preservation, and state-of-the-art benchmark performance are retained.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges the Reality-total LPIPS tie with Switch, interprets the new SDXL experiment as evidence of backbone generalisation, and leaves broader SDXL and flow-matching evaluations to future work. Section 6 qualifies the runtime limitation by explaining batching, while retaining limitations involving adapter quality and base-model artefacts.

D1.justification: New Table 10 identifies all 22 existing LoRAs, their categories, trigger words, and source links. Appendix C explicitly discloses that comparison methods share the proposed optimisation objective while replacing the fusion mechanism. v3 also explains batching and supplies a project-page link instead of a future code-release promise; the PDFs do not establish actual code availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds DreamCatalyst and LoRWeB, distinguishes its reference-free setting from example-guided composition, and explains LoRWeB's exclusion from evaluation. It removes the standalone classifier-free-guidance and DDPM references. The broader positioning between diffusion editing and LoRA composition remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method description, and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten around CDS. The method gains explicit optimisation and weighting subsections, pose analysis and ablation sections exchange order, and the supplementary material is reorganised into lettered appendices. This substantially changes exposition beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with widespread figure/table resizing and relocation. Figure 1 is redesigned, GPT-4V chart panels are rearranged, and framework labels and captions change. v3 adds the SDXL figure/table and LoRA inventory table; retained wide comparison tables become visibly smaller.

improvement.justification: The LoRA inventory and explicit baseline-adaptation details improve reproducibility, while the SDXL check and expanded temperature analysis provide limited additional validation. Main results remain unchanged. These benefits support a modest net improvement, tempered by sparse SDXL protocol details and reduced legibility of wide comparison tables after reformatting.
